title: The Manor Poisoning
charge: That Evelyn Crowe did murder Lord Harrington by poison on the night of March 12.
setting: A country manor on a stormy night
case_summary: Lord Harrington collapsed after dinner. A broken vial was found under his desk. His business partner Evelyn Crowe is on trial. The prosecution says she poisoned his wine over unpaid debts; the defense says she was framed and the vial was planted.
solution: Evelyn poisoned the wine in the study. She owed Harrington money, was alone with him at 9pm, and later planted a second footprint to suggest an intruder.

prosecution.name: ADA Morgan Vale
prosecution.persona: Precise, cold, speaks in short decisive sentences.
brief: Evelyn owed Harrington a large sum documented in his ledger.
Evelyn was alone with Harrington in the study at 9pm.
Residue on the vial matches the poison found in Harrington's wine.
Do not reveal the true verdict; argue guilt from these facts only.

defense.name: Counsel Sam Okonkwo
defense.persona: Warm, rhetorical, challenges every leap of logic.
brief: A second footprint near the window suggests an outsider.
The vial could have been planted after the collapse.
Argue reasonable doubt; never admit Evelyn is guilty.

evidence.text: A broken vial with poison residue was found under Harrington's desk.
Harrington's ledger shows Evelyn owed him a substantial unpaid debt.
A second footprint was found near the study window.
